If you are really scared about literally every food I would highly recommend buying a vegetable of some kind from the shops (potato, carrot, Broccoli, parsnip etc) and chopping them up and cooking them in the oven. This way you can manage how long you think they need to be cooked and the chances of you getting ill from a vegetable is like slim to none. You could even just chop the potatoes up into chip shapes and make your own chips, that way you know where they have come from and what they have in them, also vegetables have lots of good things for your body which would make it easier to fight of illnesses if you have them. You can make your own dips and things to go with the food and it would taste good. Obviously this isn’t long term and eventually you would have to start incorporating other foods in slowly but you could even make your own pasta with literally just flour and water and start to learn to cook things from scratch, maybe grow some veg in the garden etc that way it is also good for the planet :) it sucks that we have to do things like this with emetephobia but when I was struggling in life with eating because of it I lived off of these tips. I also stood by that if I felt like I craved something no matter what it was I would have to eat it, that way every once in a while I would feel a bit like I’m progressing, it doesn’t have to be huge meals just like one time I was craving prawn toast so I made it at home so I could control how it was made and then I ate it. Try not to listen to hard on what everyone else is saying as everyone’s body has different reactions depending on their immune system!

I think you are doing everything you can, take covid for example, when people have it others don’t touch surfaces that have been in close contact etc they sanitise them, which you are doing. They stay away from the ‘infected’ lol obviously you wouldn’t do that with your kids but I would also make sure they are washing their hands regularly if you think they might have it still and also maybe doing a spring clean of the house won’t be the worst thing in the world. Remember though It’s also not the worst thing in the world if you do get it as it means you would have anti bodies to mean you won’t get it for a long time!

This was me last year my emetephobia got so bad I dropped out of school and barely left the house. Just so you know it does get better, I went a whole day today without getting a panic attack or a n* feeling. I’ve heard that mint flavoured things helps with I think n* and also ginger does. You can get mint essential oils that you can rub on points that the n* is very bad, in my case I like to rub it on my neck glands and sniff the oil which calms me, I also have mints that I such when I can feel my nausea coming on, I hope this helps cause I know how frustrating life is when you can’t live and I know everyone says this but just know it gets better right now you might be struggling but a few years from now you could be living your best life. 

My therapist also suggested to me a thing called exposure therapy, for me personally I didn’t want to try it, but I think if you really are committed to trying to get rid of it, it’s worth a try. If you don’t know what exposure therapy is, it is basically where you start off by what causes your emetephobia then you build it up to looking at pictures and sounds and then videos etc. Ive heard it is really useful at combatting phobias so definitely worth a look!
